title: Command Atelier and Execution Handoff
summary: Quarterly leadership update focused on execution handoffs for Q4 priorities, hiring tempo, a brief incident postmortem, and runway/ops alignment. Open Q&A included product tradeoffs around Dedicated vs Private, and an action plan for a cross-functional blitz week.
action_items: Avery Chen - Draft Q4 execution RACI and share with leadership - due 2026-09-29
Jamal Ortiz - Prepare short brief on Dedicated vs Private customer signals + recommended messaging - due 2026-09-28
Priya Singh - Run two production regressions for KV cache patch and report impact numbers - due 2026-09-25
Sofie Müller - Publish hiring prioritization doc and adjust recruiter briefs - due 2026-09-24
Liam Gomez - Schedule infra cost deep-dive with finance and engineering (30m) - due 2026-09-30
next_steps: Leadership to review the RACI and confirm owners by next Tuesday
SEs to prepare a customer-facing FAQ for Dedicated vs Private positioning
Run the KV cache regression on staging then a small canary in prod
HR to re-prioritize org hiring plan and update job reqs
Finance to circulate runway slide and sensitivity scenarios
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Location: All-hands (virtual)
Attendees: Evelyn, Avery, Jamal, Priya, Liam, Sofie, many teammates in chat

[00:00] Evelyn Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining a little early, appreciate folks dialling in from, uh, tokyo and dublin. we wanted to run a tight 55 minute update — highs and lows, then q&a.
[00:10] Avery Chen: yeah, i'll kick off with the Q4 priorities and then jamal will walk through product tradeoffs. quick housekeeping — slides are up: https://redwood.ai/slides/q4-command-atelier
[00:25] Jamal Ortiz: ok, first slide — we have three top-line deliverables: 1) dedicated capacity launch improvements, 2) private deployment onboarding flow and 3) cost-optimization toolkit (optimize). each has a primary owner assigned. note: priorities are sequence sensitive bc of capacity and sales cycles.
[00:48] Priya Singh: real quick on 1), research has a KV-cache micro-optimization that cut tail latency in perf tests, but the patch introduced higher eviction in a specific path, we rolled it back friday. we need regression numbers to be confident for re-rollout.
[01:12] Liam Gomez: yeah, infra noticed a cache eviction spike around long-context sessions, that matched an autoscaler bump and we had some drop-in throughput. priya can you confirm the region? i saw it on eu-west-1.
[01:28] Priya Singh: yep, eu-west-1, and small subset in us-west-2 but staging didn't show it which is weird — maybe a workload profile mismatch.
[01:39] Avery Chen: this is the incident recap: short lived, customer impact low but noisy. two action items: regression runs and a small canary in prod with throttled traffic.
[01:53] Sofie Müller: hiring note — we pushed 18 reqs this quarter, recruiter pipeline is thin in infra and se roles. i'll propose a hiring blitz week next month to accelerate; want leaders to lock top 6 roles.
[02:12] Evelyn Park: on runway and budget: finance put together three scenarios, base/optimistic/constrained. at current burn we have 14 months base case, with changes in hiring and cloud spend we can push to 18. finance will share the slides. any major timing constraints from sales?
[02:36] Jamal Ortiz: sales is expecting Dedicated beta in time for two mid-market deals end of november, so delivery timelines are sticky. that argues for focused engineering allocation now vs later.
[02:52] [Audience question via chat] "How are we messaging Dedicated vs Private to customers that ask about data residency?"
[03:02] Jamal Ortiz: good q — short answer: Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation on our cloud, Private for full customer-managed network and on-prem options. we need a crisp decision tree doc.
[03:18] Priya Singh: also to add, from an ops standpoint Private introduces more support burden; we should price in onboarding hours.
[03:30] Evelyn Park: agreed — jamal, priya, work with finance to model TCO for customer types.
[03:41] Avery Chen: another operational ask — we need to standardize runbooks and SLA page updates. se team to own a month-by-month update cadence.
[03:55] Liam Gomez: on the KV cache regression: i'll slot a team to run a synthetic workload that mimics longer chats with token distributions. we'll instrument percentiles and evictions.
[04:10] Priya Singh: reminder: perf tests may not capture real-world prefix caching patterns. we should include production trace sampling in the regression.
[04:28] Jamal Ortiz: ok shifting to product calendar — we propose a 'blitz week' Oct 11-15 where squads get timeboxed objectives: two measurable outputs each (docs, experiments, or infra changes). leaders to nominate owners.
[04:45] Sofie Müller: note on org health — we're seeing more meetings; leadership to try a focus-hour policy twice a week to protect engineering time.
[05:02] Evelyn Park: quick shoutouts — team that handled the eviction regression rolled a rollback and triaged fast. thanks.
[05:12] [15:30 — mid meeting, Q&A open floor with mixed speakers and chat interruptions]
[15:31] Speaker 1: what's the priority if we have to pick between reducing latency tail vs reducing cost by more aggressive quantization?
[15:40] Jamal Ortiz: tradeoff: aggressive quant can save ops cost but may shift quality. for product-facing customers we bias latency/quality, for some internal analytics embeddings we can bias cost. need customer segmentation.
[15:55] Speaker 2: are we leaning into precompiled kernels vs dynamic for new models?
[16:04] Liam Gomez: both — precompiled kernels for stable families, dynamic for experimental families. scheduling chooses at deploy time. small blip: someone in transcript said "keys cache" as kv-cache, occassional misspellings.
[16:20] Jamal Ortiz: also, reminder that our rollout and fallback policy should be visible in the console so customers can choose fallback tiers.
[16:38] [Noise, crosstalk]
[17:02] Evelyn Park: wraps — recapping the asks: owners to confirm by next week, run regressions, finalize messaging on Dedicated vs Private, hiring blitz, finance runway scenarios. we'll send a shorter email w/links.
[17:20] Evelyn Park: ok final q&a — any major blockers?
[17:25] Jamal Ortiz: one blocker: a vendor dependency for a kernel optimization, vendor schedule slipped. se to evaluate alternate path.
[17:40] Sofie Müller: hiring blocker — offer acceptance delays; we need quicker interview debriefs.
[17:50] [Wrap up]
[17:55] Evelyn Park: thanks everyone, meeting ended. note: recording and transcript will land in the #all-hands channel.

Notes about transcription: some speaker labels are generic, a few proper nouns got mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" -> "keys cache"), punctuation and paragraphing are approximate, there are occasional filler words and overlapping talk.
